products.name: Falcon
products.captures: Stills of vehicles, plate text and state, vehicle description
products.not: No live video, no faces, no audio
products.note: Standard, Wide-Range and Long-Range variants; the Long-Range is sold for highways at $5,000 a year

products.name: Falcon Flex
products.captures: The same as the Falcon, on an internal battery of 14 amp-hours (about 30,000 reads per charge), with 16 gigabytes of storage to hold reads before they upload
products.not: No solar panel by default; clamps to a pole

products.name: Sparrow
products.captures: The same system, marketed to homeowners’ associations and apartment complexes for their entrances
products.not: Private customers cannot see law enforcement data; they can share their own

products.name: Condor
products.captures: Live and recorded video through two lenses, one wide (90 degrees) and one with a 32-times zoom; software that detects and follows people
products.not: Not a plate reader by itself; Flock's statement that its cameras focus on vehicles rather than people refers to the plate readers

products.name: Raven
products.captures: Rolling windows of about three seconds of audio, analyzed on the device for gunshots; Flock says only clips of events are uploaded
products.not: Flock states it cannot interpret speech; a feature that listened for human distress, which Flock says it tried with a small number of customers, was removed in July 2026

products.name: Wing
products.type: Software and gateway for existing cameras
products.captures: Plates and vehicle descriptions from the video of network cameras a customer already owns
products.not: No new camera; the one setup that uses network cables and fiber

products.name: Alpha (drone as first responder)
products.captures: Live video and plate reads from the air
products.not: Different product; folded into the same FlockOS platform

products.name: Nova
products.captures: Data fusion from public records, open-source intelligence and commercial datasets, linking a plate to a registered person
products.not: No hardware; 404 Media reported in May 2025 that Flock stated it would not use breached-data sources
